interest: Reveals intense internal Occupation clashes, labor official resignations, and Cold War diplomatic disputes over Japanese public employees' rights.
overview: This file documents the origins, implementation, and international fallout of the July 1948 directive by General Douglas MacArthur restricting collective bargaining and strike rights for Japanese civil servants through revisions to the National Public Service Law and Cabinet Order No. 201. Spanning July 1948 to September 1949, the records encompass high-level Occupation policy debates, including the protest resignation of GHQ Labor Division Chief James S. Killen, extensive Japanese press and labor union reactions, and subsequent Diet passage under the Yoshida Cabinet. It also details intense Cold War diplomatic confrontations in the Far Eastern Commission and Allied Council for Japan, featuring formal protests by the Soviet Union and British Commonwealth representatives alongside interagency negotiations between the U.S. State, Army, and Labor Departments over public corporation workers' rights and civil service political neutrality.
